meta.title: SK Hynix — Kwak Noh-Jung's HBM-leadership memory pure-play through the AI infrastructure cycle
meta.abstract: SK Hynix Inc. is a South Korean memory semiconductor company listed on the Korea Exchange (KRX: 000660). Headquartered in Icheon, South Korea, SK Hynix is the world's second-largest DRAM memory producer (after Samsung Electronics) and one of the principal global NAND flash memory producers. Within the broader SK Group conglomerate the company sits as the principal SK Group semiconductor subsidiary following the 2012 SK Group acquisition of Hynix Semiconductor (then a creditor-controlled distressed company emerging from the 2001-2002 Hynix workout period). The corporate trajectory through 2012-2026 has been substantially shaped by the multi-decade Hynix-and-subsequent-SK-Hynix DRAM business positioning, the broader NAND flash memory business positioning, the 2021 acquisition of the Intel NAND and Solidigm SSD business for approximately USD 9 billion (closed first phase December 2021, full closing December 2025), and more recent strategic positioning as the principal scaled HBM supplier to Nvidia across the HBM3 and HBM3E product cycle providing the principal AI infrastructure cycle positioning. Under CEO Kwak Noh-Jung (since March 2024, succeeding Park Jung-ho who continues as Vice Chairman) the strategic mandate has been the HBM leadership continuation, the broader memory business trajectory, and the broader strategic posture refinement. Fiscal 2024 revenue was approximately KRW 66.2 trillion (~USD 50 billion) reflecting the substantial HBM contribution plus the broader memory cycle recovery.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
SK hynix (KRX: 000660) posted KRW 23.4673 trillion in fiscal 2024 operating profit on KRW 66.1930 trillion of revenue, a turn from the KRW 7.7303 trillion operating loss on KRW 32.7657 trillion of revenue in fiscal 2023. By fiscal 2025 the recovery had extended into a second record year: revenue reached KRW 97.1467 trillion and operating profit KRW 47.2063 trillion, both the highest in the company's history. [SK hynix Announces 4Q24 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-announces-4q24-financial-results/) [SK hynix Announces FY25 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-announces-fy25-financial-results/)

The mix shift behind those numbers was visible in the company's own disclosures. SK hynix said HBM accounted for more than 40 per cent of total DRAM revenue in the fourth quarter of 2024, and then said HBM revenue more than doubled year on year in 2025. By the first quarter of 2026, revenue had risen to KRW 52.5763 trillion, operating profit to KRW 37.6103 trillion and the operating margin to 72 per cent, while cash and cash equivalents reached KRW 54.3 trillion and net cash KRW 35 trillion. [SK hynix Announces 4Q24 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-announces-4q24-financial-results/) [SK hynix Announces FY25 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-announces-fy25-financial-results/) [SK hynix Announces 1Q26 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/q1-2026-business-results/)

Kwak Noh-Jung had not, in fact, taken over in 2024. SK hynix's own CEO and governance pages showed him as president and chief executive from March 2022, with a first board appointment dated March 2022; they also showed that he had joined Hyundai Electronics in 1994 and held a Ph.D. in materials engineering from Korea University. The ownership page as of the frozen window showed 728,002,365 listed shares outstanding and SK Square as the largest shareholder with 146,118,388 shares, or 20.5 per cent. [SK hynix CEO](https://www.skhynix.com/company/UI-FR-CP0301/) [SK hynix Board of Directors](https://www.skhynix.com/sustainability/UI-FR-SA1502/) [SK hynix Ownership Structure](https://www.skhynix.com/ir/UI-FR-IR04/)

## The Cycle That Made the Case

Fiscal 2023 was the steepest memory cycle downturn in a decade. Post-COVID inventory unwinding collided with the AI-cycle pre-spend gap to produce a KRW 7.73 trillion operating loss — the worst annual result of the modern company's history. Fiscal 2024 was the mirror image: the sharpest single-year recovery on record, driven by HBM premiums that the commodity DRAM market could not replicate.

| Fiscal Year | Revenue (KRW T) | Operating Profit (KRW T) |
|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 44.62 | 6.81 |
| 2023 | 32.77 | (7.73) |
| 2024 | 66.19 | 23.47 |
| 2025 | 97.15 | 47.21 |

That momentum ran well into 2026. For Q1 2026, SK hynix reported revenue of KRW 52.5763 trillion — the first quarter in company history above KRW 50 trillion, and up 198 per cent year on year — with operating profit of KRW 37.6103 trillion and a 72 per cent operating margin, an all-time high for any reporting period. The company said the jump came from higher sales of HBM, high-capacity server DRAM modules and eSSDs despite the normal seasonal slowdown in the first quarter, and it said 2026 investment would rise materially to support M15X, the Yongin cluster and key EUV equipment. [SK hynix Announces 1Q26 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/q1-2026-business-results/)

## Solidigm and the NAND Flank

SK hynix completed phase one of its Intel NAND acquisition on 29 December 2021, paying US$7 billion for the SSD business and Dalian NAND flash manufacturing facility and launching the new San Jose-based subsidiary Solidigm under Rob Crooke, Intel's former senior vice president. The second phase was no longer prospective by the frozen date: Intel told the SEC that it closed the second phase on 27 March 2025 and collected about US$1.9 billion of proceeds, net of certain adjustments, ending the interim manufacturing-and-sale arrangement that had governed the transition. [SK hynix completes the First Phase of Intel NAND and SSD Business Acquisition](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-completes-the-first-phase-of-intel-nand-and-ssd-business-acquisition/) [Intel Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 29, 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086325000074/intc-20250329.htm)

## The Central Tension

The company's structural question was straightforward to state and difficult to resolve. SK hynix shipped 12-layer HBM4 samples to major customers in March 2025, said in September 2025 that it had completed development and preparation for mass production, and said in its FY2025 results that large-scale HBM4 production was already under way to meet customer requests. NVIDIA, for its part, had unveiled the Vera CPU and Rubin GPU roadmap at GTC in March 2025, making clear that the next platform step would require a faster memory subsystem. The commercial issue by the frozen date was therefore no longer whether HBM4 existed, but whether SK hynix could turn its early engineering lead into another cycle of high-volume, high-margin supply without a repeat of the sharp commodity reversion that had defined prior memory booms. [SK hynix Ships World’s First 12-Layer HBM4 Samples to Customers](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-ships-world-first-12-layer-hbm4-samples-to-customers/) [SK hynix Completes World’s First HBM4 Development and Readies Mass Production](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-completes-worlds-first-hbm4-development-and-readies-mass-production/) [SK hynix Announces FY25 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-announces-fy25-financial-results/) [NVIDIA Accelerated Computing Platform Roadmap](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-accelerated-computing-platform)

Whether the 2024-to-2026 profit cycle represents a structural elevation or the sharpest inflection in a long mean-reverting industry remains the central question for any investor holding the name. SK Hynix's HBM lead has compressed the answer considerably — but it has not eliminated it.

chapters.title: From Hyundai Electronics through creditor workout to SK Hynix
chapters.body:
## Hyundai Electronics: Scale as Strategy (1983–1999)

SK Hynix's origins lie not in the semiconductor ambitions of a technology company but in the industrial logic of a Korean conglomerate that believed memory chips were a commodity business best won through sheer manufacturing scale. Hyundai Electronics was established in 1983 as a division of the Hyundai Group, the sprawling chaebol whose portfolio already spanned shipbuilding, construction, and automobiles. The founding premise — that Korea could build world-class DRAM fabs by combining cheap capital, disciplined labour, and relentless capacity investment — proved durable even if the corporate structures that incubated it did not.

Through the late 1980s and 1990s, Hyundai Electronics built successive generations of DRAM fabs, tracking the technology node cadence from the then-dominant 1-micron generation toward the sub-0.25-micron processes that defined the late-decade mainstream. The company was capital-intensive and leverage-dependent in the fashion common to Korean heavy industry, running fabrication operations with debt loads that would have been unusual for Western technology peers but were normalised within the chaebol financial model. By the late 1990s, Hyundai Electronics had established itself as one of a handful of globally scaled DRAM producers alongside Samsung Electronics, Micron Technology, and Germany's Infineon — subscale on margins, formidable on volume.

## The Big Deal and the Breaking Point (1999–2001)

In 1999, the Korean government's post-financial-crisis industrial restructuring programme — the so-called Big Deal — forced a consolidation of the domestic semiconductor industry. LG Semicon, the memory operation of LG Group and the fourth significant Korean DRAM producer, was merged into Hyundai Electronics on terms dictated by the state rather than the market. The transaction added manufacturing capacity, headcount, and intellectual property, but it also added leverage to a company already strained by the late-1990s DRAM price collapse and the aftershocks of the 1997 Asian financial crisis.

The combined entity entered the 2001 global DRAM downturn — itself worsened by the technology-sector correction following the dot-com bust — carrying debt obligations that its operating cash flow could no longer service. In late 2001, the company entered a formal creditor workout, the Korean corporate restructuring mechanism administered by creditor banks rather than a bankruptcy court. SK hynix's own history page recorded 2001 as the year of separation from Hyundai Group, the step that made the Hynix identity durable. [SK hynix History](https://www.skhynix.com/company/UI-FR-CP05) The moment marked the end of the Hyundai Group chapter and the beginning of a decade of creditor-controlled independence.

## Workout: Survival Under Creditor Control (2001–2012)

Korea Exchange Bank emerged as the lead creditor institution, guiding Hynix Semiconductor through successive rounds of debt restructuring, asset disposal, and operational rationalisation across the following decade. The workout era was neither swift nor comfortable. Hynix survived three distinct memory cycle downturns — the 2001–2002 bust, the 2007–2008 NAND-and-DRAM correction, and the 2008–2009 global financial crisis shock — each of which threatened to overwhelm a balance sheet still carrying workout-era legacy obligations.

The legal environment was equally hostile. Hynix Semiconductor faced significant intellectual property litigation from Rambus Inc., the memory interface licensing company that pursued DRAM producers aggressively through the 2000s. The Rambus litigation alleged that Hynix had engaged in anti-competitive conduct and infringed on Rambus's patented memory interface technologies; it consumed management attention and legal resources across multiple jurisdictions for years before being settled. The resolution removed a material litigation overhang that had complicated Hynix's credit profile and deterred potential acquirers.

Through the workout decade, Hynix Semiconductor's management focused on the core DRAM manufacturing competency, continuing to invest in process node migration even as the balance sheet constrained capital allocation. The company was not a technology laggard when the workout ended: its 30-nm and sub-30-nm DRAM node development kept pace with Samsung and Micron, and its NAND operations, though smaller than Samsung's, maintained commercial viability. What Hynix lacked was the strategic ownership and capital structure to invest at the scale required to compete for technology leadership rather than merely technology parity.

## The SK Group Acquisition: KRW 3.4 Trillion and a Strategic Wager (2012)

In November 2011, SK Group announced that an SK Telecom-led consortium had signed the share-purchase agreement for the creditor stake in Hynix Semiconductor. SK hynix's history page recorded the subsequent launch into SK Group in March 2012, while the company's later corporate materials consistently framed the deal value at roughly KRW 3.4 trillion. [SK hynix History](https://www.skhynix.com/company/UI-FR-CP05) [SK hynix Fact Sheet](https://news.skhynix.com/corporate/fact-sheet/)

The strategic rationale was layered. SK Telecom, then Korea's dominant mobile carrier, needed assured supply of mobile DRAM as smartphone penetration across Korea and Asia accelerated. At the group level, SK Chairman Choi Tae-won identified memory semiconductors as the category most likely to generate the durable free cash flows required to fund SK Group's broader industrial transformation over the following decade. The acquisition provided vertical integration into a component that touched every device across SK Telecom's customer base while positioning SK Group in the one sector of Korean industry where Samsung had built an advantage that felt permanent.

At KRW 3.4 trillion for a creditor-controlled workout survivor with a history of cyclical operating losses, the price was considered aggressive. Memory cycle timing was unfavourable: the announcement coincided with a severe DRAM downturn, and Hynix's balance sheet carried structural liabilities from the workout era. Critics within the Korean financial community questioned whether SK Group was acquiring a liability rather than an asset. The subsequent thirteen years rendered that criticism historically irrelevant — the 2012 acquisition stands as one of the most consequential conglomerate dealmaking decisions in modern Korean industrial history, measured by the EBITDA generation that followed.

## Building Scale in the SK Era: Fabs, Capex, and the NAND Diversification (2012–2021)

Under SK Group ownership, SK hynix began a sustained programme of capital investment that the workout era had structurally prevented. The company completed M15 in Cheongju in October 2018 and broke ground for M16 at its headquarters in Icheon in December 2018; the history page then recorded completion of M16 in February 2021. [SK hynix History](https://www.skhynix.com/company/UI-FR-CP05) The M15 and M16 investments represented the most significant capacity expansion in the company's history, positioning SK hynix to compete for NAND scale while deepening its advanced DRAM base at Icheon.

The NAND ambition found its fullest expression in October 2020, when SK hynix announced the acquisition of Intel's NAND and SSD business for US$9 billion across two phases. The first phase closed on 29 December 2021, transferring the SSD business and Dalian fab for US$7 billion; the second phase closed on 27 March 2025, when Intel told the SEC it had transferred the remaining NAND technology and manufacturing business and collected about US$1.9 billion of proceeds, net of certain adjustments. [SK hynix completes the First Phase of Intel NAND and SSD Business Acquisition](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-completes-the-first-phase-of-intel-nand-and-ssd-business-acquisition/) [Intel Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 29, 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086325000074/intc-20250329.htm)

The acquired business was organised into Solidigm Technology, a US-headquartered subsidiary based in San Jose, California, led by Rob Crooke, the former Intel senior vice president and general manager of Intel's Non-Volatile Memory Solutions Group. Solidigm gave SK Hynix a credible position in the enterprise NAND SSD market, a customer base spanning hyperscale data centre operators, and an Intel-derived technology lineage distinct from SK Hynix's internal NAND development — a strategic hedge against the commoditisation pressure bearing down on the broader NAND market.

## Kwak's Appointment and the HBM Mandate

SK hynix's own history page recorded that Kwak Noh-Jung was appointed as the company's "independent representation" in March 2022, and a March 2022 anniversary release identified Park Jung-ho as vice chairman and co-CEO alongside Kwak as president and co-CEO. By the frozen window, the governance and CEO pages identified Kwak as CEO and president with a first appointment date of March 2022. [SK hynix History](https://www.skhynix.com/company/UI-FR-CP05) [On the 10th Anniversary of SK hynix Launch, Vice Chairman Park Pledges to Build Next 100 Years Together](https://news.skhynix.com/on-the-10th-anniversary-of-sk-hynix-launch-vice-chairman-park-pledges-to-build-next-100-years-together/) [SK hynix CEO](https://www.skhynix.com/company/UI-FR-CP0301/) [SK hynix Board of Directors](https://www.skhynix.com/sustainability/UI-FR-SA1502/)

Kwak's appointment carried a specific institutional logic. He had joined Hyundai Electronics in 1994, risen through manufacturing and technology posts, and most recently served as president and head of manufacturing technology before becoming CEO. The company biography gave him a Ph.D. in materials engineering from Korea University, not a KAIST doctorate in electrical engineering. [SK hynix CEO](https://www.skhynix.com/company/UI-FR-CP0301/) [SK hynix Board of Directors](https://www.skhynix.com/sustainability/UI-FR-SA1502/)

That distinction mattered because the HBM cycle was, above all, a manufacturing contest. Park's 2021-2022 co-CEO period helped frame the strategic pivot, including the Solidigm integration and the push into AI memory, but the primary-source record by 2026 showed the operating franchise clearly centred on Kwak. [SK hynix completes the First Phase of Intel NAND and SSD Business Acquisition](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-completes-the-first-phase-of-intel-nand-and-ssd-business-acquisition/) [SK hynix CEO](https://www.skhynix.com/company/UI-FR-CP0301/)

## Thirteen Years: From Workout to Industry Pivot

The numerical testimony of the SK Group era requires little editorial elaboration.

| Fiscal Year | Revenue (KRW T) | Operating Profit/(Loss) (KRW T) |
|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 26.99 | — |
| 2020 | 31.90 | — |
| 2021 | 42.99 | — |
| 2022 | 44.62 | 6.81 |
| 2023 | 32.77 | (7.73) |
| 2024 | 66.19 | 23.47 |

*Source: [SK Hynix IR financial information](https://www.skhynix.com/eng/ir/financial-information)*

The KRW 23.47 trillion operating profit posted in fiscal 2024 — a KRW 31 trillion year-on-year swing from the prior year's loss — was the steepest single-year recovery in the company's recorded history, driven by SK Hynix's position as principal scaled HBM supplier to NVIDIA.

SK Hynix entered SK Group in February 2012 as a workout survivor. It closed fiscal 2024 as the largest SK Group subsidiary by market capitalisation — a return on KRW 3.4 trillion that reshaped the global memory industry's competitive geography.

chapters.title: DRAM, HBM, NAND, and Solidigm
chapters.body:
## A Portfolio Repriced by One Product Family

SK hynix still described itself in the conventional way: a supplier of DRAM, NAND flash and CMOS image sensors. But by the frozen window, the company's financial record showed that the important distinction sat inside DRAM rather than across the legacy product buckets. In the fourth quarter of 2024, SK hynix said HBM had risen to more than 40 per cent of total DRAM revenue. For full-year 2025, it said HBM revenue had more than doubled year on year. In the first quarter of 2026, it again attributed record results to HBM, high-capacity server DRAM modules and eSSDs. [SK hynix Announces 4Q24 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-announces-4q24-financial-results/) [SK hynix Announces FY25 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-announces-fy25-financial-results/) [SK hynix Announces 1Q26 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/q1-2026-business-results/)

The right way to read the business, therefore, was as three legacy segments increasingly reorganised around one strategic premium line: HBM inside DRAM.

## DRAM: Still the Core Business

DRAM remained the group's central manufacturing franchise even after the HBM boom changed the mix. The ordinary DRAM portfolio still covered server memory, mobile memory, graphics DRAM, PC memory and consumer products, and the company's 2024–2026 releases repeatedly referred to DDR5, LPDDR, GDDR and server-module roadmaps alongside HBM. [SK hynix Reports Financial Results for 2023, 4Q23](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-reports-fourth-quarter-2023-financial-results/) [SK hynix Announces FY25 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-announces-fy25-financial-results/)

What changed was the value hierarchy inside that portfolio. Conventional server DRAM still mattered because it kept fabs full and supported the cost structure of the broader DRAM franchise. In FY2025, the company highlighted the development of a 256GB DDR5 RDIMM built on 32Gb fifth-generation 10nm-class DRAM, underscoring that high-capacity server modules remained part of the core proposition. In 1Q26, it said it would fully ramp shipment of LPDDR6 built on the 1cnm process and a 192GB SOCAMM2 module based on the same process. [SK hynix Announces FY25 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-announces-fy25-financial-results/) [SK hynix Announces 1Q26 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/q1-2026-business-results/)

The mobile and graphics lines were evolving in parallel. In March 2026, SK hynix announced development of 1c LPDDR6 with 33 per cent faster speed and more than 20 per cent better power efficiency than LPDDR5X. In July 2024, it introduced GDDR7 and said mass production would begin in the third quarter, presenting the product as a graphics and AI-adjacent memory line with materially better speed and power efficiency. [SK hynix Develops 1c LPDDR6, 6th-Generation 10nm-Class DRAM](https://news.skhynix.com/1c-lpddr6-development-2026/) [SK hynix Enhances Leadership in Graphics Memory With Introduction of Industry’s Best GDDR7](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-enhances-leadership-in-graphics-memory-with-introduction-of-industry-best-gddr7/)

## HBM: The Premium Layer Inside DRAM

HBM was the line that changed the economics of the whole group. SK hynix's own historical materials showed a long runway rather than a sudden opportunistic jump. The fact sheet recorded the world's first HBM in 2013, HBM3 development in 2021 and HBM3 mass production in 2022. The product milestones then accelerated with the AI build-out: 8-layer HBM3E mass production in March 2024, 12-layer HBM3E volume production in September 2024, 12-layer HBM4 sample shipments in March 2025 and completion of HBM4 development in September 2025. [SK hynix Fact Sheet](https://news.skhynix.com/corporate/fact-sheet/) [SK hynix History](https://www.skhynix.com/company/UI-FR-CP05) [SK hynix Begins Volume Production of the World’s First 12-Layer HBM3E](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-begins-volume-production-of-the-world-first-12-layer-hbm3e/) [SK hynix Ships World’s First 12-Layer HBM4 Samples to Customers](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-ships-world-first-12-layer-hbm4-samples-to-customers/) [SK hynix Completes World’s First HBM4 Development and Readies Mass Production](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-completes-worlds-first-hbm4-development-and-readies-mass-production/)

By early 2026, the company was no longer discussing HBM4 as a laboratory milestone. It told investors that large-scale HBM4 production was already under way to meet customer requests, while still presenting HBM3E and HBM4 side by side as the AI memory portfolio. [SK hynix Announces FY25 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-announces-fy25-financial-results/) [SK hynix Showcases HBM4 & Next-Gen AI Memory at COMPUTEX Taipei 2025](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-showcases-hbm4-next-gen-ai-memory-at-computex-taipei-2025/)

## NAND and the Solidigm Layer

NAND remained a structurally different business from DRAM, but it was no longer a peripheral one. SK hynix's 2022 and 2024 product releases documented progress from 238-layer 4D NAND to 321-high 4D NAND with 1Tb capacity. In 1Q26, management again highlighted demand for high-capacity eSSDs, indicating that the storage line was being positioned as an AI-adjacent complement to HBM rather than as a standalone commodity bet. [SK hynix Develops World’s Highest 238-Layer 4D NAND Flash](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-develops-worlds-highest-238-layer-4d-nand-flash/) [SK hynix Starts Mass Production of World's First 321-High NAND](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-starts-mass-production-of-world-first-321-high-nand/) [SK hynix Announces 1Q26 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/q1-2026-business-results/)

The Solidigm acquisition altered the commercial orientation of the NAND unit. Phase one of the Intel NAND deal closed on 29 December 2021, creating the US-headquartered Solidigm subsidiary; Intel's March 2025 quarter-end filing said the second closing occurred on 27 March 2025. By the frozen window, enterprise SSD and AI-storage positioning belonged inside the integrated business rather than in a still-pending transaction category. [SK hynix completes the First Phase of Intel NAND and SSD Business Acquisition](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-completes-the-first-phase-of-intel-nand-and-ssd-business-acquisition/) [Intel Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 29, 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086325000074/intc-20250329.htm)

## CIS: Retained but Subscale

CMOS image sensors remained part of the official product list, but the company's own capital-allocation language made their relative importance clear. The expansion agenda published in 2025 and 2026 centred on HBM, server modules, eSSD, LPDDR6, GDDR7, M15X, Yongin, Cheongju packaging and Indiana packaging. CIS survived as an adjacent category, not as the line around which management was organising incremental investment. [SK hynix Announces FY25 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-announces-fy25-financial-results/) [SK hynix Announces 1Q26 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/q1-2026-business-results/)

## Manufacturing Footprint as Segment Strategy

The physical footprint also mapped directly to the business mix. The history page recorded M15 in Cheongju, M16 in Icheon and the first fab in the Yongin cluster as the major front-end capacity markers. The Indiana release described a separate US$3.87 billion advanced-packaging fabrication and R&D facility in West Lafayette, while the FY2025 release said advanced-packaging sites in Cheongju and Indiana were progressing smoothly. Taken together, those disclosures showed a segmented manufacturing map: Korean front-end memory capacity, Korean and US back-end expansion, and a storage flank reinforced through the former Intel assets. [SK hynix History](https://www.skhynix.com/company/UI-FR-CP05) [SK hynix Signs Investment Agreement of Advanced Chip Packaging with Indiana](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-signs-investment-agreement-of-advanced-chip-packaging-with-indiana/) [SK hynix Announces FY25 Financial Results](https://news.skhynix.com/sk-hynix-announces-fy25-financial-results/)
